I’m sorry you’re dealing with that — I know how stressful it is when you need cash right away. I can help walk through a few quick checks and options so you can get cash as soon as possible. Quick questions first so I give the right advice:

1) Are you in the U.S. or traveling abroad right now?  
2) Are the ATM declines showing any error message on the screen (e.g., “DECLINED”, “PIN INCORRECT”, or “INSUFFICIENT FUNDS”)?  
3) Do any of the three cards show visible physical damage (bent/chipped/missing chip), or are any of them very new (issued within the last 24 hours)?  

While you reply, here are immediate steps and options to try now at the ATM:

- Try a different ATM (preferably a Rho‑Bank ATM or a bank-branded ATM). Sometimes a terminal/owner fee or terminal flag will block withdrawals at that machine.  
- Try inserting the chip if you were swiping (or vice versa), or try contactless tap if the card supports it — chip/stripe issues can cause declines.  
- Don’t request cash back from a purchase terminal (some declines happen if cash back isn’t allowed). Try a straight ATM withdrawal only.  
- If your teen’s Light Green (teen) card: note the ATM daily limit is $150 — if you’ve already hit that the machine will decline.  
- Blue Account debit card: the daily ATM limit is $500; if you’ve done withdrawals earlier today you may have hit the limit.  
- Green Account (no‑overdraft): withdrawals will be declined if there isn’t enough available balance (this account will not overdraft).  

Other immediate options if ATM still won’t work:

- If you have the Rho mobile app or online access, you could:
  - Send a quick EveryonePay transfer to someone you trust who can withdraw cash for you (EveryonePay has a daily limit of $250).  
  - Move funds between your accounts in the app (if you have another account with available ATM access).  
- Ask a nearby branch teller (if there’s a bank branch nearby) if they can give a cash withdrawal against your card or account — branches can sometimes help with immediate cash if you can verify identity in person.  
- If you think this is a security/hold or fraud block (multiple cards declined at once or rapid declines), we can transfer you to a human agent right away to check for holds or security blocks on the accounts.

If you’d like me to escalate now, I can transfer you to a human agent who can check for security holds and card status immediately. Would you like me to do that, or do you want to try any of the troubleshooting

I’m in the U.S. (Denver).

The ATM screen just said “transaction declined” or something like that — I didn’t see a specific code.

No, the cards aren’t damaged and they’re not brand new. What do we do next?

Thanks — that helps. Since you’re in the U.S. and the ATM only showed a generic “transaction declined,” the most likely causes are: a temporary terminal/ATM issue, hitting an ATM/daily limit on one or more cards, or a security/hold placed by the bank because of multiple rapid declines. Because three different cards declined, I recommend we check for any security holds or per-card limits right away.

You have two options — pick whichever you prefer:

Option A — I can look up the card/account statuses now
- I’ll need to verify your identity first because I’ll be viewing account/card information. Per our process, please confirm any two of the following: date of birth, email on the account, phone number on the account, or your mailing address. (Do not include your full SSN.)  
- After you provide two, I’ll run the checks and tell you if there are holds, daily-limit usages, or other reasons for the declines and next steps to get access to funds.

Option B — Quick immediate actions you can try right now (no verification needed)
- Try a different ATM (preferably a Rho‑Bank or other bank-branded ATM). Terminal flags sometimes block a specific machine.  
- Try a different withdrawal amount (smaller amount) — if a daily limit was nearly reached, a smaller withdrawal may go through.  
- For your teen’s card: remember Light Green accounts have a $150/day ATM limit.  
- If you have the Rho app: send an EveryonePay to a friend or family member who can withdraw cash for you (EveryonePay limit is $250/day), or transfer between your own accounts if available.  
- If there’s a nearby Rho branch, go inside and ask the teller — they may be able to give cash if you can verify ID in person.  
- If you prefer immediate verbal help, you can call 1‑800‑RHO‑BANK and request an urgent agent to check for security holds.

Which do you want to do — should I verify you now and check for holds/limits, or would you like to try the quick steps yourself first? If you want me to check, please provide two of these: date of birth, email, phone number, or mailing address.

Immediate options you can try right now (fastest ways to get cash)
- Try a different ATM (preferably a Rho‑Bank or another bank‑branded ATM nearby). Terminal flags often block a single machine.  
- Try a smaller withdrawal amount — if you’re near a daily limit, a smaller amount may go through.  
- Go into the nearest bank branch (if there’s one close) and ask a teller for a cash withdrawal — bring your ID and the teller can help you access cash from your account.  
- If you have the Rho mobile app on your phone: send an EveryonePay to someone you trust to withdraw cash for you (EveryonePay limit is $250/day) or check the app for the last 4 digits of your card to share here.  
- Call 1-800-RHO-BANK right now and they can immediately check for holds/blocks on your cards over the phone.
